business_problem: CCC needed to train and iterate on large computer-vision models for insurance claims automation, but hybrid data movement, bursty GPU demand, and developer orchestration made it hard for data scientists to move models from experimentation to production quickly.
solution_summary: CCC built a hybrid AI development pipeline around NVIDIA DGX Cloud, NVIDIA Base Command Platform, and DGX A100 systems to support the models behind CCC Estimate-STP. The company extracts structured and unstructured claims data from its production environment into sub-lakes, anonymizes it, and manages the resulting datasets in Base Command Platform so data scientists can schedule jobs consistently across on-premises and cloud GPU resources. Base Command's open API and Kubernetes compatibility let CCC integrate scheduling and resource management directly into its internal model-development workflow, while DGX Cloud provides 24x7 access to additional GPUs whenever training demand spikes. That platform supports the computer-vision and ensemble-model experiments used to turn mobile phone photos into line-level repair estimates in seconds, instead of leaving adjusters to rely on manual workflows that can take days.

data_flow: Claims data is extracted from production into sub-lakes, anonymized and loaded into Base Command Platform, model-training jobs are scheduled across DGX A100 and DGX Cloud capacity, and the resulting computer-vision models feed CCC Estimate-STP so insurers can generate repair estimates from smartphone photos.
business_outcome: CCC reported a 2x speedup in running experiments, compressed some model-development cycles from months to days, and used the platform to launch CCC Estimate-STP, which can deliver detailed line-level collision estimates in seconds from photos instead of relying on workflows that can take several days.
